name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa / Visa-Exempt Entry

qualifying_event.description: Nationals of visa-exempt countries may enter Malta (Schengen area) without a visa; other third-country nationals require a Schengen (Type C) short-stay visa issued by Malta's Central Visa Unit or another Schengen state's mission.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Valid passport; for visa applicants: proof of purpose of visit, return travel, sufficient funds, travel/medical insurance.

requirements.blocker_text: Maximum stay of 90 days within any 180-day period under the Schengen short-stay rule. Does not permit employment or study — separate permits are required for those purposes, and exempt nationals wishing to stay beyond 90 days must apply for a Maltese National (long-stay) visa.

evidence_required.document: Schengen (Type C) visa, if not visa-exempt

outcome.duration_length: up to 90 days within any 180-day period

sources.title: Identità -- Central Visa Unit: Schengen short-stay visa policy, 90/180-day rule, visa-exempt nationalities, employment/study restriction, National Visa for longer exempt stays

notes: NEW ROUTE, first route of Malta's initial build. Malta has been a full Schengen member since 2007. Confirmed directly at tier-1. switchable_to left empty: the source does not describe an in-country conversion path from a short-stay Schengen visit directly into a residence permit category -- applicants for work/study/family routes are generally expected to apply through the Expatriates Unit before or shortly after arrival, not to convert an existing short-stay visa in-country. dual_citizenship_allowed reflects Malta's general policy (Malta permits dual/multiple citizenship), not something specific to this route.
